title: Balinese Kingdom
capsule: Following the Majapahit conquest of 1343, the Kepakisan dynasty installed as vassal rulers gradually asserted independence as Majapahit itself faded, and from its palace at Gelgel in southeastern Bali the kingdom reached its apogee under Dalem Baturenggong, who extended Gelgel's suzerainty over Lombok, western Sumbawa, and Blambangan in eastern Java while resisting the Islamization spreading across the archipelago. His successors Dalem Bekung and Dalem Seganing weathered court rebellions and failed expeditions against Java, and the dynasty's authority collapsed after 1651 when the chief minister Gusti Agung Maruti usurped power at Gelgel. The old line's heir, Dewa Agung Jambe I, reestablished the court at Klungkung around 1686, though he could no longer command the whole island, which fractured into competing lordships.
